_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (mTNBC) who have received at least two prior therapies for metastatic disease.

pivotal_trials.design: Single-arm, multicenter (US only), non-randomized, open-label trial in patients with advanced solid tumor malignancies.
pivotal_trials.population: 108 patients with mTNBC who received a starting dose of 10 mg/kg on Days 1 and 8 of every 21-day cycle after at least two prior lines of therapy for metastatic disease.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Objective response rate (ORR) by RECIST 1.1 and duration of response.
pivotal_trials.result: Confirmed investigator-assessed ORR 33.3% (95% CI: 24.6, 43.1); median duration of response 7.7 months (95% CI: 4.9, 10.8).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥25%) were nausea, neutropenia, diarrhea, fatigue, anemia, vomiting, alopecia, constipation, rash, decreased appetite, and abdominal pain. In the efficacy population, the most common (≥20%) AEs by preferred term were nausea (69%), neutropenia (64%), diarrhea (63%), fatigue (57%), anemia (52%), vomiting (49%), alopecia (38%), constipation (34%), rash (31%), decreased appetite (30%), and abdominal pain (26%). Grade 3-4 AEs occurred in 72.2% of patients, most commonly neutropenia (43%). Serious AEs occurred in 33%, most commonly infection (9%) and febrile neutropenia (8%).
target_moa: A Trop-2-directed antibody-drug conjugate: the humanized anti-Trop-2 antibody (hRS7 IgG) is conjugated via a CL2A linker to SN-38, a topoisomerase I inhibitor; upon binding and internalization, released SN-38 inhibits topoisomerase I, causing DNA damage and apoptosis.

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for neutropenia and diarrhea: severe neutropenia may occur (withhold for ANC below 1500/mm3 or neutropenic fever, monitor CBC, consider G-CSF and anti-infectives) and severe diarrhea may occur (monitor, give fluids/electrolytes, atropine for early diarrhea, loperamide for late diarrhea).

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an advisory committee; the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues unexpected for a biologic of this class or in the intended population.
